radial_light — GFX2D light op

• Data kinds: कोई नहीं → rgb (केवल arguments से तय होने वाला op — यह कोई image या data input नहीं लेता)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.radial_light(height, width, x, y, radius, intensity=1.0, falloff='smooth', color='emphasis', scheme='okabe_ito') (implementation को सीधे call करना हो तो import gfx2d; gfx2d.radial_light(height, width, x, y, radius, intensity=1.0, falloff='smooth', color='emphasis', scheme='okabe_ito'), registry से लेना हो तो opsgfx2d.get("radial_light"))

उपयोग

radial light map, rgb (H, W, 3), (x, y) पर केंद्रित।

> नीचे का विस्तृत विवरण मूल text में है — सारांश और headings का अनुवाद हो चुका है।

falloff:

• "smooth" — (1 - t^2)^2, compactly supported: exactly zero at and beyond radius. The default, because a light that ends somewhere is the only kind you can budget.

• "linear" — 1 - t, also compact.

• "inverse_square" — 1 / (1 + (3t)^2), the physical law softened at the origin. Not compactly supported: it is 10 % of peak at the nominal radius and never reaches zero, so a scene full of these never gets dark.

The value at the centre is exactly intensity * color. This is a *linear-light* quantity: add lights together, then encode once.

With intensity > 1 the result leaves [0, 1] — deliberately, because a light map is not a picture. light_mask accepts it; the operators that take an rgb *image* reject it with the documented range error rather than clipping a light budget behind your back.
